newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-RAYTHEON DEAL SPARKS STRENGTH.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-RAYTHEON DEAL SPARKS STRENGTH.

text.p: Spreads on investment-grade corporate bonds tightened Thursday as a successful $3 billion debt offering from Raytheon Co generated increased demand in the overall market, traders said.
Prices of junk bonds were also up about a quarter of a point, lead by strength of in new issues one trader said.
"The market feels stronger for corporate debt in general, on the heels of the Raytheon offering," a trader said.
A spokesman for the defense contractor said: "Investor interest was quite high and we think this is an endorsement of our strategy and where the company is headed."
The company's offering, rated Baa1/BBB, included three-, five-, ten- and 30-year bonds and was priced via a syndicate which included over 15 different investment-banks.
New issuance of investment-grade corporates also picked up soon after the Raytheon offering, traders said.
Bristol Meyers priced $300 million of 100-year debentures (AAA/AAA) to yield 6.905 percent and Staples Inc (Baa3/BB-plus) priced $200 million in 10-year notes to yield 7.155 percent.

Other issuers on Thursday included Hollywood Entertainment Corp with a $200 million offering, ValuJet Airlines Inc with a $80 million deal, WinStar Equipment Corp with a $50 million deal and Atlantic Express Transportation Corp with a $40 million offering.
Grand Union Co bonds were volatile Thursday over continued concerns about the company's ability to make an upcoming interest payment, a trader said.
A Grand Union spokesman confirmed that several suppliers have "pulled the plug" on deliveries to the supermarket gaint amid concerns about its ability to meet its debt obligations.
The one area of weakness among high-grades, was the trust preferred stock sector, a trader reported.
Spreads there widened by several basis points on concerns that increased volatility in Treasuries would hurt trust preferreds because they are callable securities, he said.
In the high-yield bond sector, a flury of new issues priced on Thursday. Several were increased in size due to strong demand in the market.
ICN Pharmaceuticals priced $275 million in debt at par to yield 9.25 percent. The deal, which was heard increased from $200 million, was trading a 102 later in the day.

"There's less than a handful of other suppliers who have been frightened by the media reports -- that are not necessarily true -- that have ceased some terms but we are working with them to get those terms back in order," he said.
In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 71.31 points to 8188 on Thursday.
U.S. Treasury priced ended markedly lower on THursday, as retail customers shunned the afternoon's 30-year bond auction, forcing deals to substantially cheapen up the issue late in the session.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury dropped 20/32 to 101-8/32, pushing its yield up to 6.50 percent.
